summary: Friedrich Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick (~1873–1876), later holding posts at Göttingen (~1878–1895) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1895–1924).

Friedrich Bollensen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen (~1827–1830), later holding posts at Gatchina Orphanage (1834), Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1860), and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Haag worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (~1865–1869, habilitation 1873), Berlin, and Göttingen, before serving as Dozent at Zurich (1873–1884) and professor at Bern (~1878–1914).

Friedrich Hirth specialized in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig (~1865–1866), Berlin (~1866–1867), and Greifswald (~1867–1869), and later held a post at Columbia University (~1902–1917).

Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, Franz Bopp, and others. He spent his career at Oxford from 1850, becoming professor in 1854.

Friedrich Müller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Theresianum, University of Vienna, and Göttingen, studying under Anton Boller (~1853–1856). He worked at Austrian libraries and printing offices before becoming professor at Vienna (1869).

Friedrich Rückert specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Franz Bopp, and later served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826) and Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig, and later under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at Jena (~1799–1801), Cologne (~1804–1807), and TU Dresden.
Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under August Conrady (~1912–1915) and served as Ordinarius for Indology at Leipzig University from 1928.

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798), Würzburg (~1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1820–1827), Munich (~1827–1841), and Berlin (~1841–1846).

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg, and subsequently held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1833), Breslau (~1833–1839), Bonn (~1839–1865), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Munich and Bonn (PhD ~1832–1833) under Christian Lassen, later holding posts at Munich (~1836–1858) and as vicar general for the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1848–1861).

Friedrich Zarncke was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1843–1847) and later held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1850–1852) and Leipzig University (~1852–1891).

Friedrich von Spiegel worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen, Hermann Brockhaus, and Heinrich Fleischer, and held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1849–1890).

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam and Banaras Hindu University, later holding posts at the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967), MIT (~1967–1968), and UC Berkeley (~1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1919–1923), later holding posts there (~1934–1941) and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Nagoya University (-1991) under Musashi Tachikawa, Yusho Miyasaka, and other teachers, and was attested as a lecturer at Chiba College of Health Science in 1991.

Fumihiko Sueki works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1978), where he served as professor (attested 1988–2003), later holding posts at Nichibunken and SOKENDAI (~2009–2014).

Fumimaro Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1953–1960) and held posts at Ryukoku, Hanazono University, Nagoya University, and Aichi Gakuin University (~1982–1990).
